description: Task Builder page -- a specialized editor for creating and managing task definitions (also known as prompts internally). Tasks define automation work units with a name, content body containing AI instructions or prompt text, category, and tags. They serve as reusable prompt building blocks that can be referenced from workflow agentic steps, providing consistent AI instructions across multiple workflows without duplication.

groups.name: Task Library Management
groups.description: The left panel displays all saved tasks in a searchable list following the standard library builder layout. Each task item shows its name, category badge, a content preview (first 60 characters of the prompt text), and tag count. Users can browse the list, search by name, create new tasks, and select a task to load into the editor. The UI labels this as 'Tasks' though the underlying API uses 'prompts' as the resource name.

assertions.description: Users see the Tasks page title within the standard library builder layout, identifying this as the task/prompt management interface
Users can create a new task definition, opening a blank editor with empty name, content, and category fields ready for input
Users can search through saved tasks by name to quickly locate specific prompt definitions in their library
Each task in the list shows a content preview of the first 60 characters of the prompt text, helping users identify tasks without opening them in the editor

groups.name: Task Editor and Content
groups.description: The right-panel editor provides fields for defining a task. The name field identifies the task in lists and pickers. The content field is a textarea for entering the full prompt text or AI instructions -- this is the most important field as it defines what the AI should do when this task is used in a workflow. An optional category field supports organizational grouping. Tags can be added for flexible labeling. The editor toolbar includes save and delete actions.

assertions.description: Users can set a descriptive name for the task that identifies it in library lists, dashboard results, and workflow step pickers
Users can write the full prompt text or AI instructions in a content textarea, defining the automation work that this task represents when used in workflows
Users can save the task definition to the library, making it available for reference in workflow agentic steps and discoverable through the library dashboard
Users can assign a category to the task for organizational grouping (e.g., 'Generation', 'Debugging', 'Code Review'), aiding discovery across the library

groups.name: Organization and Discovery
groups.description: Tasks support tags for flexible cross-cutting labeling that enhances discovery through the library dashboard and search. The tag input allows adding multiple tags using an enter-to-add pattern and individual tag removal. Combined with categories, tags create a rich organizational system that scales with library growth. The delete action allows users to remove outdated or unused task definitions.

assertions.description: Users can add and remove tags on tasks, providing flexible labels for cross-category discovery and filtering in the library dashboard
Users can delete task definitions they no longer need, keeping their library clean and relevant
The task list shows the number of tags on each item, helping users identify well-organized tasks at a glance

states.name: Loading — Fetching Tasks
states.description: Initial state while the page fetches saved task definitions from the prompts API endpoint. A loading indicator is displayed in the list panel.

transitions.name: Tasks loaded
transitions.description: The API fetch completes and at least one task exists, populating the left-panel list

transitions.name: No tasks exist
transitions.description: The API fetch completes but no task definitions were returned

states.name: Empty Library — No Tasks Exist
states.description: No task definitions have been created yet. The list panel is empty and the user is prompted to create their first task using the New button.

transitions.name: Create first task
transitions.description: User clicks the New button to open a blank task editor, beginning their first task definition

states.name: List Ready — Tasks Loaded, No Selection
states.description: The left-panel list is populated with saved tasks showing name, category badge, content preview, and tag count. No task is currently selected for editing in the right panel. The search box and New button are available.

transitions.name: Create new task
transitions.description: User clicks the New button to open a blank editor with empty name, content, and category fields

transitions.name: Select existing task
transitions.description: User clicks a task in the list to load it into the right-panel editor for viewing or modification

transitions.name: Enter search query
transitions.description: User types in the search box to filter the task list by name

states.name: Editing — Task Loaded in Editor
states.description: A task is loaded in the right-panel editor, either a new blank task or an existing one selected from the list. The editor shows the name field, content textarea for prompt text, category field, and tag management. The toolbar provides Save and Delete actions. The left-panel list remains visible for navigation.

transitions.name: Save task
transitions.description: User clicks Save to persist the task definition, returning to the list which now reflects the saved changes

transitions.name: Delete task
transitions.description: User clicks Delete to remove the task definition, returning to the list with the deleted task removed

transitions.name: Switch to another task
transitions.description: User clicks a different task in the list, replacing the editor contents with the newly selected task

transitions.name: Create new task while editing
transitions.description: User clicks New to discard the current editor contents and start a fresh blank task definition

states.name: Search Active — Filtering Task List
states.description: The user has entered a search query in the search box, filtering the left-panel task list by name. Matching tasks are displayed; non-matching tasks are hidden.

transitions.name: Clear search query
transitions.description: User clears the search input to return to the full unfiltered task list

transitions.name: Select task from filtered results
transitions.description: User clicks a task from the filtered search results to load it into the editor

transitions.name: No matching tasks
transitions.description: The search query does not match any tasks, showing an empty results state

states.name: Empty Results — No Matching Tasks
states.description: The search query does not match any saved tasks. The list panel shows an empty state message. The user can clear the search to restore the full list.

transitions.name: Clear search to restore list
transitions.description: User clears the search input to return to the full task list
